finding: R32 blocked: GStreamer state-change deadlock under high pipeline churn
upstream_reference: Eyevinn/strom#963 — independently reported lock-order deadlock in uridecodebin3/typefind (GStreamer 1.28.6) with the same two-thread signature: typefind streaming thread waiting for the state lock while the control thread's set_state waits for typefind's stream lock. No fixed build is available in the repositories (cachyos-extra-v3 gstreamer = 1.28.7-2.1, the installed version).

soak_attempts.outcome: wedge while loading pcm24_192000.wav; DAC held
wedge while loading pcm16_48000.wav; no ALSA fd
wedge while loading pcm16_44100.wav; no ALSA fd; subprocess-isolated characterizer + Qt offscreen did not prevent it; workers cycled cleanly
aborted: Wayland session loss broke the Qt app (offscreen introduced for attempt 5)

workarounds_untested: settling gap — wait for the previous state change to complete before starting the next (suggested in the upstream report); not yet validated in the lab
root_cause: gst_element_change_state (pipeline set_state) recurses through pad activation and blocks forever on a pthread_mutex held by a stuck streaming thread (typefind/wavparse/multiqueue in futex_wait). gst_pad_pause_task is the last resolvable frame; the characterizer timeout (pipeline.get_state with a 5 s budget) does not interrupt the wedge (the sibling thread sits in g_cond_wait_until).
reproduction: Directed stress harness (two isolated source-characterizer hammer threads at >300/s plus the lab's load/stop churn) reproduces a permanently stuck pipeline in about 11 seconds; the frozen counter and lingering typefind/wavparse/multiqueue threads are the signature. The harness's own faulthandler watchdog captured all-thread Python stacks, and a py-spy parent run (no ptrace needed) captured native stacks.
impact: Any process that churns GStreamer pipelines (the 8 h R32 soak creates ~200k pipelines at ~7/s; the app also exposes it because Direct staging/stop state operations run on the main thread) can hang permanently with no timeout protection. Three soak attempts ended this way (power loss excluded, two wedges: 189k and 148k cycles).
sibling_stack_frozen_thread: characterize_local_file [gstreamer.py:384 get_state] -> g_cond_wait_until (the 5 s timeout does not return)
main_thread_exposure: async prepare completion is delivered to the main thread (qt_async_call.py QueuedConnection) and performs pipeline staging (output_session_service.py _prepare_request -> direct_output_executor.prepare -> gstreamer.py stage_direct_load); stop/load state requests are also main-thread (gstreamer.py _request_state -> set_state).

isolation_experiments.name: two characterizer churn threads, no app playback
one characterizer churn thread only
isolation_experiments.result: WEDGED within ~47 seconds; a single pipeline's own state transition can deadlock, so serialization alone does not eliminate the hazard

isolation_experiments.name: app-style direct load/stop churn only (~7/s)
isolation_experiments.result: survived 8 minutes / 3485 cycles; the race is rare per lifecycle but scales with pipeline count (the 8 h soak wedged at 148k/189k lifecycles)

upstream_report: upstream-report.md (ready to file; gitlab.freedesktop.org search is protected by Anubis)
options_considered: Serialise all GStreamer lifecycle/state operations under one process-wide lock and quarantine stuck pipelines from a watchdog (product mitigation).
Change the R32 lab stress profile (slower cadence or periodic engine lifecycle resets) via a canonical decision.
Report upstream to GStreamer with the captured native stacks.
decision: R32 stays NOT_RUN; the physical verdict remains INCOMPLETE. No further long runs until a separate project decision.
